option_1_compact_map_callback.strategy: keep accepted prefix byte-for-byte; preserve the five stage names once, then explain only the missing/unique functions while referring back to the already-explained middle rather than restating it
option_1_compact_map_callback.candidate_text:
I use five stage names for the movement: the child alone, the child with a borrowed adult, the adult apprentice, the inner adult, and the adult and child in relationship. I put those five stages together myself. Some of the pieces have direct research behind them, but the sequence as a whole is still provisional.

The first step is getting oriented to the present and making the outside situation safe enough to begin. The middle is what I just described: borrowing one reliable adult function from someone real, remembered, imagined, or symbolic, then taking pieces of it yourself while support is still there. Warmth, protection, and direction become easier to call up with repetition. At the other end, the adult can lead without pushing the child away, and the child no longer has to run the whole life alone.

You don’t have to stop being the child. “I am still this child, and I am also becoming the adult who stays.”
option_1_compact_map_callback.strongest_objection: the opening still exposes a five-name taxonomy and the first/middle/other-end compression may remain visibly schematic
option_1_compact_map_callback.best_repair_if_that_objection_is_real: use Option 2, which removes the separate taxonomy block and lets stage labels arise from the continuous developmental movement
option_1_compact_map_callback.editorial_tradeoff: best compromise if stage names need to remain skimmable without repeating five full definitions

option_3_reallocate_progression_to_map.map_text:
I think of the whole process in five stages. I put the sequence together myself. Some of the pieces have direct research behind them, but the five-stage arrangement is still provisional:

1. The child alone — get oriented to the present and make the outside situation safe enough to begin.
2. The child with a borrowed adult — get one reliable adult function from someone real, remembered, imagined, or symbolic.
3. The adult apprentice — do the caring with support and take one part yourself.
4. The inner adult — keep repeating warmth, protection, and direction until you can call them up more easily.
5. The adult and child in relationship — the adult leads without pushing the child away, and the child doesn't have to run the whole life alone.

You don’t have to stop being the child. “I am still this child, and I am also becoming the adult who stays.”
option_3_reallocate_progression_to_map.strongest_objection: the visible numbered map still has inherently regular structure and this option reopens a prefix that already passed five times
option_3_reallocate_progression_to_map.best_repair_if_that_objection_is_real: prefer Option 2 unless the explicit skimmable numbered map is important enough to justify changing the accepted prefix
option_3_reallocate_progression_to_map.editorial_tradeoff: cleanest way to preserve an actual numbered practical map without explaining the same developmental sequence twice
